title: LLM Complexity: Towards a Computational Complexity View of Large Language Model Inference
abstract: arXiv:2611.24943v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Computational complexity theory offers a principled framework for characterizing the efficiency of computational problems, and Large Language Models (LLMs) can similarly be viewed as computational systems executing a structured process of input, inference-time compute, and output. In this context, the number of generated tokens emerges as a natural and directly observable proxy for inference-time compute. However, we show that the tempting analogy between LLM token length and classical time complexity does not hold. We disprove the hypothesis that inference-time token usage aligns monotonically with classical time complexity, demonstrating a fundamental divergence grounded in how LLMs actually allocate computation during inference. To this end, we introduce LLM Complexity, a new metric designed to quantify problem complexity from the perspective of LLMs by characterizing the area bounded above by the accuracy-token curve. translated_abstract: 计算复杂度理论为刻画计算问题的效率提供了一个原则性框架，而大语言模型（LLM）同样可以被视作执行“输入—推理时计算—输出”这一结构化过程的计算系统。在此背景下，生成token的数量成为衡量推理时计算量的一个自然且可直接观测的代理指标。然而，我们证明了LLM token长度与经典时间复杂度之间这一颇具吸引力的类比并不成立。我们否定了“推理时token使用量与经典时间复杂度单调一致”这一假设，并展示了其根本性分歧源于LLM在推理过程中实际分配计算的方式。为此，我们提出了LLM复杂度（LLM Complexity）这一新指标，通过刻画准确率-token曲线所界定的面积，从LLM的视角量化问题复杂度。我们发现……
tldr: 该论文证明LLM推理时的token使用量与经典时间复杂度并非单调对应关系，并提出“LLM复杂度”这一新指标，通过准确率-token曲线下的面积从LLM的视角量化问题复杂度。
en_tdlr: This paper disproves the hypothesis that inference-time token usage aligns monotonically with classical time complexity, and introduces "LLM Complexity," a new metric that quantifies problem complexity from the LLM's perspective via the area bounded by the accuracy-token curve.
